jurisdiction.name: Switzerland
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Switzerland has no AI-specific law. In February 2025 the Federal Council decided to ratify the Council of Europe AI Convention and to make targeted sector-specific changes to Swiss law rather than adopt horizontal AI legislation, based on OFCOM's AI overview report and a legal analysis by the Federal Office of Justice; the consultation draft for ratification was not yet open in October 2026. The revised Data Protection Act (in force September 2023) applies directly to AI, including a duty to inform about automated individual decisions, as the data protection commissioner has confirmed, and automated driving has been regulated since March 2025. In the federal administration the Federal Council's 2020 AI guidelines, the 2025 AI sub-strategy with its implementation plan, a Competence Network for AI created by ordinance in 2026, and staff guidance on generative AI set the rules. FINMA's 2024 guidance sets supervisory expectations for AI governance in finance, and Swiss standards adopt ISO/IEC 42001. The cantons of Zurich, Geneva, Vaud, Basel-Stadt and Bern have their own AI guidelines and strategies, and Zurich is preparing a register of algorithmic decision systems.
lead_institutions: Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 11 October 2026, covering federal laws and ordinances, the Federal Council and federal administration, the data protection commissioner, FINMA, the Competition Commission, Swissmedic, national standards, and the cantons of Zurich, Geneva, Vaud, Basel-Stadt and Bern. Searches were made in German, French, Italian and English. Swiss standards were read from the national standards body's catalogue entries, as their full texts are sold. Council of Europe and other international instruments are recorded in the regional files. Pending: the consultation on ratifying the Council of Europe AI Convention, the draft law on communication platforms and search engines, Zurich's revised information law and its register of algorithmic decision systems, and parliamentary motions on deepfakes and AI and copyright.

instruments.official_title: Strategie Einsatz von KI-Systemen in der Bundesverwaltung
instruments.english_title: Strategy for the use of AI systems in the federal administration (AI sub-strategy)
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Chancellery, Digital Transformation and ICT Steering sector (DTI)
instruments.current_status: Core document of the Federal Chancellery's page on AI in the federal administration (footer 'Teilstrategie – Gültig per 21.03.2025'). Approved by the Delegate for Digital Transformation and ICT Steering (DTI) on 17 March 2025; the Federal Council was informed on 21 March 2025. French title: « Stratégie relative à l'utilisation de systèmes d'IA dans l'administration fédérale ». Implemented through an implementation plan. It is a strategy, not law; the military's mission-critical AI is outside the DigiV (Art. 5).
instruments.summary: Sub-strategy (federal IT requirement SB021) under the Digital Federal Administration Strategy that applies to all AI systems used in the federal administration, whatever the field or technology. It sets a vision, five principles (human-centred and trustworthy, integrated and cross-cutting, clear accountability, sustainable, reliable and robust) and twelve prioritised goals in three fields of action: building skills, earning trust (lifecycle governance of AI systems, safe use of sensitive data, assessing generative AI) and increasing efficiency (AI planning by administrative units, legal bases for partial or full automation such as first-instance rulings, shared standard services). It has no fixed validity period and is to be revised by 2030 at the latest.

instruments.official_title: Bundesgesetz über den Datenschutz (Datenschutzgesetz, DSG)
instruments.english_title: Federal Act on Data Protection (Data Protection Act, FADP)
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Assembly of the Swiss Confederation
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 September 2023 (Federal Council decision of 31 August 2022; text 'Inkrafttreten: 1. September 2023'). Adopted by the Federal Assembly on 25 September 2020; published in the Official Compilation as AS 2022 491 on 6 September 2022. Consolidated version read: 'Stand am 7. Juli 2025' (Fedlex consolidations 2023-09-01, 2025-04-01, 2025-07-07). Replaced the Federal Act on Data Protection of 19 June 1992. French title: Loi fédérale sur la protection des données (LPD). The Federal Council's AI approach of 12 February 2025 names data protection as a core cross-sector area for the forthcoming AI Convention implementation bill.
instruments.scope: Switzerland (federal); private persons and federal bodies
instruments.summary: The revised Federal Act on Data Protection (SR 235.1) governs the processing of personal data of natural persons by private persons and federal bodies and applies technology-neutrally to AI systems that process personal data. Art. 21 requires controllers to inform the data subject of any decision based exclusively on automated processing that has a legal effect on or significantly affects them, to let them state their view on request and to have the decision reviewed by a natural person (exceptions for contract decisions granting the request or explicit consent); federal bodies must label such decisions. It also regulates profiling, including high-risk profiling (Art. 5), requires data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing, notably when new technologies are used (Art. 22), and extends the right of access to the existence of automated individual decisions and the logic involved (Art. 25).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument relevant to AI governance (data-privacy, binding-law).

instruments.official_title: Verordnung über den Datenschutz (Datenschutzverordnung, DSV)
instruments.english_title: Ordinance on Data Protection (Data Protection Ordinance, DPO)
instruments.issuing_authority: Swiss Federal Council
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 September 2023; adopted by the Federal Council on 31 August 2022 (AS 2022 568, published 7 October 2022). Consolidated version read: 'Stand am 1. Dezember 2025'; the amendment of 29 October 2025 revised the logging rule for federal bodies (Art. 4(2)) with transitional deadlines of 31 December 2026 (review) and 31 December 2029 (implementation) in Art. 46. French title: Ordonnance sur la protection des données (OPDo).
instruments.scope: Switzerland (federal); private controllers and federal bodies
instruments.summary: The Federal Council's implementing ordinance to the Federal Act on Data Protection (SR 235.11) sets data-security requirements for automated data-processing systems and duties that attach to profiling. Private controllers must log processing and keep a processing regulation for automated processing where sensitive data are processed on a large scale or high-risk profiling is carried out (Arts. 4-5); federal bodies must log and keep processing regulations whenever they carry out profiling (Arts. 4 and 6) and must notify the FDPIC of planned automated processing projects (Art. 31).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument relevant to AI governance (data-privacy, binding-law).

instruments.official_title: Strassenverkehrsgesetz (SVG) (Änderung vom 17. März 2023)
instruments.english_title: Road Traffic Act (SVCA), amendment of 17 March 2023 (vehicles with an automation system)
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Assembly of the Swiss Confederation
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Federal Assembly on 17 March 2023 (AS 2023 453, published 18 August 2023); referendum period expired unused on 6 July 2023. Most provisions entered into force on 1 October 2023; Title IIa (Arts. 25a-25h) on automation systems was put into force on 1 March 2025 by the Federal Council ordinance on partial commencement of 13 December 2024 (AS 2025 49). Some other provisions (Arts. 9(3bis), 25(2bis), 52(1-2), 99a, 105a) remain to be put into force later. French: Loi fédérale sur la circulation routière (LCR).
instruments.scope: Switzerland (federal); road traffic, vehicles with automation systems
instruments.summary: This amendment of the Road Traffic Act inserts a new Title IIa 'Fahrzeuge mit einem Automatisierungssystem' (Arts. 25a-25h), defining vehicles able to take over the driving task permanently and comprehensively under certain conditions. It empowers the Federal Council to release drivers from their duties, allows driverless vehicles only on designated routes under supervision by an operator (routes set by the registering canton), and requires a non-deactivatable, tamper-proof driving-mode data recorder logging activations, takeover requests, risk-minimising and emergency manoeuvres and the installed software version.

instruments.official_title: Verordnung über das automatisierte Fahren (VAF)
instruments.english_title: Ordinance on Automated Driving (OAD)
instruments.issuing_authority: Swiss Federal Council
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Federal Council on 13 December 2024 (AS 2025 50, published 21 January 2025); in force 1 March 2025 except amendments to Annexes 11 and 12 of the Vehicle Registration Ordinance (1 July 2025). French text corrected 21 February 2025 (AS 2025 127). Amended 15 October 2025 (Art. 50(5), French and Italian text only), in force 1 January 2026; consolidated version read: 'Stand am 1. Januar 2026'. French title: Ordonnance sur la conduite automatisée (OCA). The consultation draft was opened by DETEC in 2023.
instruments.summary: The Federal Council ordinance (SR 741.59) implementing Arts. 25a-25g of the Road Traffic Act sets the conditions for the approval and use of motor vehicles with an automation system and the processing of data related to them. It defines vehicles with takeover request, automated parking systems and driverless vehicles, sets general requirements for automation systems (e.g. mastering traffic scenarios within the operational design domain per UNECE/EU methods, deactivation, accident avoidance, protection against unlawful interference), and regulates approval of automated-parking areas and of operating areas and operators for driverless vehicles.

instruments.official_title: Auslegeordnung zur Regulierung von künstlicher Intelligenz. Bericht an den Bundesrat
instruments.english_title: Overview of approaches to regulating artificial intelligence: Report to the Federal Council
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (Federal Office of Communications) with the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (State Secretariat, Europe Division)
instruments.current_status: Report dated 12 February 2025 (BAKOM-D-A5D93401/201) and submitted to the Federal Council that day; OFCOM page states the Federal Council decided the Swiss regulatory approach on this basis (press release 'KI-Regulierung: Bundesrat will Konvention des Europarats ratifizieren', 12 February 2025). Follow-up: FDJP (with DETEC and FDFA) to prepare a consultation draft implementing the Convention by end of 2026, covering transparency, data protection, non-discrimination and supervision; DETEC (with FDJP, FDFA and EAER) to prepare an implementation plan for non-binding measures by end of 2026. Neither had been published by 11 October 2026 (FOJ page; Federal Council answer of 2026 to interpellation 26.3414). Basis analyses published alongside: legal analysis, sectoral analysis ('Überblick Regulierungsvorhaben') and country analysis.
instruments.summary: Report commissioned by the Federal Council on 22 November 2023 that sets three goals for Swiss AI regulation (strengthening Switzerland as an innovation location, protecting fundamental rights including economic freedom, and strengthening public trust in AI) and compares three approaches: continuing sector-specific regulation, ratifying the Council of Europe AI Convention with minimal or broader implementation, or ratifying it with an EU AI Act-style product regulation. It draws on a legal base analysis (FOJ), a sectoral analysis of federal regulatory projects and a 20-country analysis, reviews the federal AI guidelines, and suggests examining regulatory sandboxes. On this basis the Federal Council decided on 12 February 2025 that the AI Convention is to be transposed into Swiss law with sector-specific amendments where possible, cross-sector rules limited to core fundamental-rights areas such as data protection, and complementary non-binding measures.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument relevant to AI governance (strategy, government-governance).

instruments.official_title: Rechtliche Basisanalyse im Rahmen der Auslegeordnung zu den Regulierungsansätzen im Bereich künstliche Intelligenz
instruments.english_title: Legal base analysis for the overview of regulatory approaches to artificial intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Department of Justice and Police (Federal Office of Justice)
instruments.current_status: Dated 31 August 2024 (BJ-D-F0D63401/159); published with the overview report on 12 February 2025 on the OFCOM page ('Juristische Analyse') and the FOJ AI page. An analytical document, not a decision; it is the legal basis for the FOJ's ongoing legislative project to implement the AI Convention.
instruments.summary: Legal analysis by the Federal Office of Justice (with contributions from the Directorate of International Law, OFCOM and the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property) supporting the AI overview report. It examines the obligations of the Council of Europe AI Convention and the EU AI Act and their consequences for Switzerland, and reviews selected cross-sector areas of Swiss law (including data protection, non-discrimination, liability and intellectual property). It concludes that Swiss law applies fully to AI but that amendments would be needed to ratify the Convention, and that alignment with the EU AI Act would require comprehensive legislation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument relevant to AI governance (government-governance, data-privacy).

instruments.official_title: Bundesgesetz über Kommunikationsplattformen und Suchmaschinen (KomPG) – Vorentwurf
instruments.english_title: Federal Act on Communication Platforms and Search Engines (KomPG/LPCom) – preliminary draft for consultation
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Council; consultation conducted by the Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (OFCOM)
instruments.publisher_name: Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications
instruments.current_status: Consultation opened 30 October 2025 and closed 16 February 2026 (Federal Gazette notice BBl, Fedlex consultation proj/2024/65). No dispatch (Botschaft) to Parliament found on Fedlex as of 11 October 2026. On 14 October 2026 the Federal Council took note of the consultation results (report dated 14 October 2026; press release https://www.admin.ch/de/newnsb/NMn5s24l8NjQ) and instructed DETEC (UVEK) to prepare a dispatch by the end of June 2027, adding youth-protection measures; the press release says the act is to cover very large platforms and search engines, including AI search engines. French: Loi fédérale sur les plateformes de communication et les moteurs de recherche (LPCom).
instruments.scope: Switzerland (federal); very large communication platforms and search engines
instruments.summary: Preliminary draft of a federal act imposing duties on providers of very large communication platforms and search engines to strengthen user rights and transparency. Besides notice-and-action, statements of reasons, internal complaints and out-of-court dispute settlement, it defines 'recommender system' as a fully or partly automated system that suggests or prioritises content and requires providers to disclose the main parameters of their recommender systems and their weighting in their terms, inform users of options to modify them, and offer for each recommender system at least one option not based on profiling under the Data Protection Act (Art. 18). It also requires ad labelling, ad archives, annual transparency reports to OFCOM, risk assessments and data access for researchers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument relevant to AI governance (drafts, transparency).

instruments.official_title: Umsetzungsplan KI-Teilstrategie
instruments.english_title: Implementation plan for the AI sub-strategy of the federal administration, with roadmap 2026–2028
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Chancellery, Digital Transformation and ICT Steering sector (DTI)
instruments.current_status: First published 12 December 2025 (note on the document; the Federal Council took note the same day per its press release). The version read is the update dated September 2026 (Federal Chancellery page date 18 September 2026) adding the Roadmap 2026–2028. To be reviewed by end-2028 at the latest. Funding decisions were left to the Federal Council.
instruments.summary: Sets eight measures to implement the AI sub-strategy: strengthening the Competence Network for AI (CNAI), training offers led by the Federal Office of Personnel, an AI marketplace (deferred; the CNAI project database is to be reoriented as a public and internal overview of AI systems, partly to meet the Council of Europe AI Convention's transparency needs), a handbook (dropped for now), operationalising AI principles in federal ICT governance (with SEPOS and the Federal Office for Cybersecurity), a generative AI system for the whole administration, a legal-framework report and an analysis of AI potential (postulate 24.3582). The September 2026 update adds a 2026–2028 roadmap for each measure and reprioritises them because of limited resources.

instruments.official_title: Leitlinien «Künstliche Intelligenz» für den Bund. Orientierungsrahmen für den Umgang mit künstlicher Intelligenz in der Bundesverwaltung
instruments.english_title: Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence for the Confederation: general frame of reference on the use of AI within the federal administration
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Council (prepared by the EAER/SERI with DETEC and the interdepartmental working group on AI)
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Federal Council on 25 November 2020 (date given on the Federal Chancellery and SERI pages; SERI states the Federal Council adopted them in November 2020). Still listed by the Federal Chancellery in 2026 as the general AI guidelines, and the generative-AI and LLM fact sheets state that they continue to apply; not superseded. OFCOM evaluates their application (first evaluation 2022 found no need to amend). French: « Lignes directrices sur l'intelligence artificielle pour la Confédération ».
instruments.summary: Seven guidelines adopted by the Federal Council as a general frame of reference for the federal administration and bodies performing federal administrative tasks when drafting sectoral AI strategies, adapting sector regulation, developing and using AI systems, and shaping international AI rules. They cover putting people first (fundamental rights, 'ethics by design', impact assessment for rights-sensitive applications, non-discrimination, privacy by default), framework conditions for AI, transparency, traceability and explainability, accountability, safety, active participation in AI governance, and involving all relevant national and international actors. Annexes set specific guidelines for education, research and innovation and explain that the existing legal order applies fully to AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument on AI (ethics, public-sector, government-governance).

instruments.official_title: Rechtlicher Rahmen für die Nutzung von KI in der Bundesverwaltung. Bericht in Umsetzung von Ziel 2 des Handlungsfelds 3 der KI-Teilstrategie
instruments.english_title: Legal framework for the use of AI in the federal administration (report implementing goal 2 of field of action 3 of the AI sub-strategy)
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Chancellery, Legal Section
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 dated Bern, 25 September 2026 (change log: v0.1 was an AI-generated draft of 28 January 2026). Annex C checklist published as XLSX on the same page. To be updated as the federal AI regulation bill (Federal Office of Justice) progresses.
instruments.summary: 80-page practical legal guide (with annexes A and B and a checklist, annex C) for federal staff and legal services planning AI projects. It classifies use cases by function, internal or external effect and degree of automation and autonomy, and covers the principle of legality (Art. 5 and 13 Federal Constitution; new legal bases for partial or full automation affecting citizens), procedural guarantees (investigation, right to be heard, duty to state reasons), transparency and information duties, equal treatment and non-discrimination (bias), data protection including automated individual decisions (Art. 21 FADP), official secrecy and information security (e.g. prompt injection), protection of legitimate expectations and liability. It does not replace legal advice in individual cases.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument on AI (public-sector, risk-assurance, data-privacy, transparency).

instruments.official_title: Merkblatt zur Verwendung von generativen KI-Werkzeugen in der Bundesverwaltung
instruments.english_title: Fact sheet on the use of generative AI tools in the federal administration
instruments.issuing_authority: Working group 'KI in der Bundesverwaltung' of the Competence Network for AI (CNAI), with representatives of all departments and the Federal Chancellery; published by the Federal Chancellery
instruments.current_status: Version V1.2 dated 18 January 2024 (file reference 822.1-1/8/5/1); the fact sheet states it is reviewed regularly. Earlier versions are not on the page. Listed by the Federal Chancellery in 2026 among current aids.
instruments.summary: Guidance for federal staff on public generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Bard, Grok): responsible experimentation is encouraged, but staff must never enter classified (internal, confidential, secret) information, texts covered by official or professional secrecy, or personal data of any kind; outputs must be checked and responsibility stays with the employee. Decisions based on AI output must be justifiable, and people have a right to information about automated individual decisions (Art. 21 FADP). It gives examples of permitted and forbidden uses and refers to the 2020 AI guidelines and the federal data science code of conduct.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument on AI (generative-ai, public-sector, data-privacy).

instruments.official_title: Merkblatt zur Sensibilisierung betreffend grosse KI-Sprachmodelle in der Bundesverwaltung
instruments.english_title: Awareness fact sheet on large language models in the federal administration
instruments.issuing_authority: Working group 'KI in der Bundesverwaltung' of the Competence Network for AI (CNAI), with representatives of all departments and the Federal Chancellery; published by the Federal Chancellery
instruments.current_status: Version V1.0 dated 26 April 2024 on the document; the Federal Chancellery page lists the file with the date 29 April 2026 (likely re-upload). Reviewed regularly per its footnote.
instruments.summary: Explains what large language models are and sets six principles for federal users (inspired by the UK Generative AI Framework for HMG): know the technology and its limits, use it lawfully and ethically (check the legal basis, which differs for translation support, drafting or fully automated decisions), keep use secure, ensure meaningful human control, use AI transparently (labelling AI-generated text is recommended and mandatory for automated individual decisions under Art. 21 FADP), and apply the 2020 AI guidelines and the data science code of conduct. Users should carry out an individual risk analysis before integrating generative AI into their work.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Swiss federal instrument on AI (generative-ai, public-sector, transparency).

instruments.official_title: Merkblatt DeepL Pro Translate und DeepL Write
instruments.english_title: Fact sheet on DeepL Pro Translate and DeepL Write
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Chancellery, Language Technologies Competence Centre
instruments.current_status: Dated 30 July 2025 (reference BK-D-7BD83401/126).
instruments.summary: Rules for federal staff on the AI translation and editing tools DeepL Pro Translate (procured by WTO tender for the central federal administration, Parliamentary Services and federal courts from 2024 to end-2033) and the free DeepL Write. It states that DeepL Pro is preferred to Google Translate, ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot for machine translation, sets a matrix of permitted inputs by classification level and presence of personal or sensitive data (no confidential or secret texts; DeepL Write only for unclassified texts without personal data), requires official publications to go to the language services without prior machine translation, and asks that machine-translated texts for others be checked or labelled.

instruments.official_title: Effizienzsteigerung von Verwaltungsprozessen durch Prozessautomatisierung und künstliche Intelligenz. Bericht des Bundesrates in Erfüllung des Postulates 24.3582 Silberschmidt vom 12. Juni 2024
instruments.english_title: Increasing the efficiency of administrative processes through process automation and artificial intelligence: Federal Council report in response to postulate 24.3582 Silberschmidt
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Council (prepared by the Federal Chancellery, DTI)
instruments.current_status: Report dated Bern, 2 October 2026 (Federal Council). Fulfils postulate 24.3582 of 12 June 2024. Includes German and French summaries.
instruments.summary: Federal Council report on how AI, robotic process automation and other automation can make the federal administration more efficient, drawing on practice in leading e-government countries and an AI potential analysis. It prioritises cross-departmental use cases (business management and office consultation, technology-assisted translation, examination of applications and cases, data extraction and harmonisation, back-office support processes) and sets fields of action: a clear legal framework for automation, stronger steering and coordination of scaling, process description and economic assessment, shared specialist and standard services, sound data foundations (registers, master data, interoperability) and sovereign infrastructure, reusability and change management.

instruments.english_title: Concept for developing the coordination of AI use in the federal administration (Competence Network for AI, CNAI)
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Chancellery and Federal Department of Home Affairs (Federal Statistical Office)
instruments.current_status: Dated Bern, 12 December 2025. The Federal Council took note of it on 12 December 2025 (press release 'Bund plant gezielte Massnahmen für den Einsatz von KI in der Bundesverwaltung und stärkt Koordination') and gave the network a legal basis by amending the Digitalisation Ordinance (in force 1 February 2026).
instruments.summary: Concept, based on an evaluation of the Competence Network for AI (CNAI), that keeps the network model but moves its central contact point from the Federal Statistical Office to the Federal Chancellery's DTI sector and aligns it with the AI sub-strategy and its implementation plan. It defines impact goals, operational goals, the contact point's tasks and decentralised competence units organised by theme (strategy and governance, tools and platforms, procurement, training and culture, law and regulation, cyber and information security and data protection, data science), working in four-month agile planning cycles.

instruments.english_title: Ordinance on Digital Services and Digital Transformation in the Federal Administration (Digitalisation Ordinance), amendment of 12 December 2025 (Competence Network for AI)
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Council
instruments.current_status: Adopted 12 December 2025, published in the Official Compilation (AS 2025 869) on 30 December 2025 and in force from 1 February 2026 (section III). It amends the DigiV of 2 April 2025 (SR 172.019.1), which is not itself AI-specific.
instruments.summary: Federal Council ordinance amendment (AS 2025 869) that inserts a new section 3a 'Kompetenznetzwerk für künstliche Intelligenz' (Art. 32a) into the Digitalisation Ordinance (SR 172.019.1). The network links administrative units dealing with AI use in the federal administration and consists of the internal ICT service providers, the Federal Chancellery's DTI sector, the Federal Statistical Office, the Federal Office of Personnel, the Federal Office for Buildings and Logistics, SEPOS, the Federal Office for Cybersecurity, the Federal Office of Justice, OFCOM and the FDFA Directorate of International Law; the DTI sector coordinates it and runs a contact point. It also adds SEPOS to the Digitalisation Council and repeals the FSO's former CNAI task in the FDHA organisation ordinance.

instruments.official_title: Verhaltenskodex des Bundes für menschenzentrierte und vertrauenswürdige Datenwissenschaft
instruments.english_title: Federal code of conduct for human-centric and trustworthy data science
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Council (prepared by the FDHA / Federal Statistical Office with an interdepartmental group, under the federal Data Science Strategy)
instruments.current_status: Dated Bern, 8 November 2023 (Der Bundesrat). Published on the Federal Statistical Office's asset server (bfs.admin.ch asset 29325686, cited by the AI sub-strategy). Referred to by the 2024 generative-AI and LLM fact sheets and the AI sub-strategy.
instruments.summary: Voluntary professional-ethics code for federal administrative units that use data science, explicitly including AI methods. It defines basic principles (data and information protection, information security, data security, data governance, non-discrimination, explainability, traceability, transparency, reproducibility, neutrality, objectivity and ethical handling of data and results) and sets practical questions for each step of the data science process, from problem formulation and data collection to analysis, evaluation and communication of results. It is not a binding directive but may later be developed into one; compliance is the responsibility of each unit.

instruments.official_title: Künstliche Intelligenz und internationales Regelwerk. Bericht an den Bundesrat
instruments.english_title: Artificial intelligence and international rules: report to the Federal Council
instruments.issuing_authority: Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (Directorate of International Law)
instruments.current_status: Report dated Bern, 13 April 2022; the Federal Council took note on 13 April 2022 (cited as its decision in OFCOM's 2022 monitoring report). Published as an attachment to the Federal Council press release on admin.ch.
instruments.summary: FDFA report, mandated by the Federal Council on 13 December 2019, analysing how international AI rules are emerging on five levels (international law, soft law, national acts with international reach, technical standards and corporate self-commitment, and the normative force of technology) and noting a general trend toward principle- and risk-based regulation that partly differs from the Swiss debate. leads.note: Mandated by the Federal Council on 12 February 2025 (FOJ page https://www.bj.admin.ch/de/kuenstliche-intelligenz): consultation draft (bill plus explanatory report) on new rules for the use of AI covering transparency, data protection, non-discrimination and supervision, to be submitted to the Federal Council by end of 2026. Switzerland signed the Convention on 27 March 2025. FOJ set up an advisory group (document dated 17 December 2025) and held a participatory workshop on 27 October 2025 (synthesis report 28 November 2025). The Federal Council's answer to interpellation 26.3414 (Molina, submitted 20 March 2026) confirms the draft is still being prepared and 'too early' to name concrete amendments. As of 11 October 2026 no consultation has been opened: a Fedlex search of all consultation procedures (titles and descriptions, DE/FR/IT) found none on AI, and no dispatch (Botschaft) exists. Record as consultation_draft when the Federal Council opens the consultation.
